    Module Essentials

    Collapse all Expand all

    Here you will find general information about the module and the topics that will be covered

    • Welcome to ELEC0129 - Introduction to Robotics

       

      The course is the first module of the IEP Robotics Minor. It provides a general understanding of the theory of robotic manipulator, and how industrial robots are programmed to perform automation tasks. Students will develop skills in the analysis of articulated robotic arm as well as the synthesis of complete robotic systems. 

    • Short welcome from module leader Media Resource

    • Key module information

    • Module catalogue URL

      UCL’s Module Catalogue provides summary information for all modules running at the University in the current academic year. To view the summary of this module enter the module code or keywords from its title.

    • Syllabus
      This module will cover the following topics:
      • Spatial transformations and descriptions;
      • Robot kinematics;
      • Jacobians;
      • Robot dynamics;
      • Trajectory planning;
      • Control of robots; and
      • Offline robot programming.
    • Learning Outcomes

      At the end of this module, participants should be able to:

      • Demonstrate learning of the theory of robotic manipulators for analysis and synthesis of armed robots;
      • Simulate the motion of articulated robots;
      • Control the robot arms to follow a prescribed trajectory;
      • Program an actual robotic manipulator using state-of-the-art software.

      Extenuating Circumstances

Information on submitting an EC claim can be found in the Student Handbook.

      Providing feedback on your assessed work

      Feedback concerning your work is an extremely important part of your academic development at UCL, and the Department is committed to providing appropriate support. We aim to ensure that the assessment mechanisms allow students to demonstrate the skills and knowledge they have gained and that the assessments are carried out fairly and consistently. It is a priority of the Department to provide students with suitably instructive and timely feedback. Late submission penalties are given in the Academic Manual Section 3.12 (Late Submissions).

      Turnaround time

      The Department aims to return assessed work within the period outlined in the Academic Manual Section 5.2.4 (Feedback). The feedback turnaround times are monitored by the Departmental Teaching Committee, and we expect students to have had the opportunity to reflect, and act, on their learning from the feedback in subsequent assessments.

    Overview

    There is no class this week, as year 2 students (you!) are completing the Year 2 Scenario. However, next week's material will be released this week, thus please spare some time to go through the material before the start of next week.

    Week 2: Introduction to the Course (LEC); Spatial Description and Transformations (LEC); Offline Programming (WS)

    Overview

    In this week's lectures, first, you will learn the terminologies in robotics and have an overview of the topics covered in the course. You will also learn how the course is run. Then, you will learn about descriptions of position and orientation of rigid bodies, as well as the homogeneous transformation matrix. 

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.

    • Lecture

      In this week's lectures, first, you will learn the terminologies in robotics and have an overview of the topics covered in the course. You will also learn how the course is run. Then, you will learn about descriptions of position and orientation of rigid bodies, as well as the homogeneous transformation matrix.  

      • Instructions: Please watch the pre-recorded videos, read the accompanying lecture notes, participate in the discussion forums actively, and take the quiz to check your understanding of the knowledge. These are labeled as Tasks 2.1 to 2.8 in the links below.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 1. 

      Workshop

      In this week's workshop, you will learn how to use RoboDk to program industrial robotic manipulator to perform automation tasks. You will then be briefed on the robot programming assessment.

      • Instructions: Please follow the workshop instruction (Task 2.9) during the workshop. You will also need to download the CAD files (Task 2.10) to be used with the software. 
      • Date, time and venue: 
        • Monday of Week 2 (11am-1pm) if your student number ends with 0-4.
        • Wednesday of Week 2 (9am-11am) if your student number ends with 5-9.
        • MPEB 6th Floor Lab.


      Expected learning outcomes

      At the end of this session, participants should:

      • Understand how positions and orientations of rigid bodies are described. 
      • Understand how to map the positions and orientations of rigid bodies in different frames.
      • Understand how to perform transformation arithmetic.
      • Understand how to program an industrial robot using the offline programming method.

      Suggested Schedule

      Please complete the asynchronous activities (Tasks 2.1 to 2.8) below before the workshop (Tasks 2.9 to 2.1-).

      If possible, please print out the workshop instruction notes (Task 2.9) or bring a second device to show the instructions, so that you do not have to switch between screens when you attend the workshop.

    Week 3: Spatial Description and Transformation (LEC & TUT); Build Robot (WS)

     

    Overview

    In this week's lectures, you will learn how to calculate the inverse of the 4 x 4 homogeneous transformation matrix. You will also learn four other interpretations of the rotation matrix, namely fixed angles, Euler angles, equivalent angle-axis and Euler parameters.

     

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.

    • Lecture

      In this week's lectures, you will learn how to calculate the inverse of the 4 x 4 homogeneous transformation matrix. You will also learn four other interpretations of the rotation matrix, namely fixed angles, Euler angles, equivalent angle-axis and Euler parameters.

      • Instructions: Please watch the pre-recorded videos, and read the accompanying lecture notes. These are labeled as Tasks 3.1 to 3.8 in the links below.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 2.

      Tutorials

      In this week's tutorials, we will solve the tutorial questions on the topic of spacial description and transformation.

      • Instructions: Please try to solve the tutorial questions on the final few pages of the lecture notes (Task 3.9). Then, please refer to the written answer in Task 3.10, and/or the recorded videos in Task 3.11 to 3.19.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 2.

      Workshop

      In this week's workshop, you will build your robots. If you have time after completing the robot, you may also work on your RoboDK assignment.

      • Instructions: You will go through tasks 3.20 to 3.22 together during the workshop. 
      • Date, time and venue:
        • Everyone to attend both sessions: Monday  (11am-1pm) and Wednesday (9am-11am).
        • MPEB 6th Floor Lab.

      Expected learning outcomes

      At the end of this session, participants should:

      • Understand how to calculate the inverse of the 4 x 4 homogeneous transformation matrix.
      • Understand four alternative interpretations of the rotation matrix, namely fixed angles, Euler angles, equivalent angle-axis and Euler parameters.
      • Understand how to calculate the fixed angles, Euler angles, equivalent angle-axis and Euler parameters, given a rotation matrix with numerical values.


      Suggested Schedule

      Please complete Tasks 3.1 to 3.8 below, and attempt to solve the tutorial questions (Tasks 3.9 to 3.19) before the workshop  (Tasks 3.20 to 3.22).

    Week 4: Forward Kinematics (LEC, TUT & WS)

    Overview

    In this week's lectures, you will learn about forward kinematics, i.e. given the joint space parameters and robot parameters, where is the position of end-effector in Cartesian space. Then in this weeks' workshop, you will derive the forward kinematics for your robot.

     

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.

    • Lecture

      In this week's lectures, you will learn how to calculate the position and orientation of the end-effector in Cartesian space, given the joint space parameters and physical parameters of the robot. You will learn about frame attachment and Denavit-Hartenberg parameters, and how these lead to the answer on the position and orientation of end-effector. 

      • Instructions: Please watch the pre-recorded videos, and read the accompanying lecture notes. These are labeled as Tasks 4.1 to 4.13 in the links below.
      • Date of video release:  Latest by Friday of Week 3.

      Tutorials

      In this week's tutorials, we will solve the tutorial questions on the topic of forward kinematics.

      • Instructions: Please try to solve the tutorial questions on the final few pages of the lecture notes (Task 4.14). Then, please refer to the written answer in Task 4.15, and/or the recorded videos in Task 4.16 to 4.19.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 3.


      Workshop

      In this week's workshop, you will derive the forward kinematics of your robot.

      • Instructions: You will go through tasks 4.20 together during the workshop. 
      • Date, time and venue: Monday of Week 4 (11am-1pm) AND Wednesday of Week 4 (9am-11am), MPEB 6th Floor Lab.

      Expected learning outcomes

      At the end of this session, participants should:

      • Understand how to attach frames on various parts of the robot,
      • Understand how to derive the Denavit-Hartenberg parameters of the robot,
      • Understand how to calculate the transformation matrices between neighboring frames, and
      • Understand how to calculate the position of the end-effector with respect to the base frame.


      Suggested Schedule

      Please complete Tasks 4.1 to 4.13 below, and attempt to solve the tutorial questions (Tasks 4.14 to 4.19) before the workshop  (Tasks 4.20).

    Week 5: Inverse Kinematics (LEC & TUT); Offline Programming (WS)

    Overview

    In this week's lecture and tutorial sessions, you will learn how to solve the inverse kinematics question, i.e. calculate the joint space parameters, given the desired position and orientation of the end-effector or the n-th frame. Then in the workshop hours, you will have time to complete your offline programming assignment.

     

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.


    • Lecture

      In this week's lecture, you will learn how to solve the inverse kinematics question, i.e. given the desired position and orientation of the end-effector (or the last frame), what should the joint space parameters be to achieve the desired outcome? Despite the fact that there is no general algorithm to solve the inverse kinematics problem, you will learn 3 techniques which are often very useful.

      • Instructions: Please watch the pre-recorded videos, and read the accompanying lecture notes. These are labeled as Tasks 5.1 to 5.10 in the links below.
      • Date of video release:  Latest by Friday of Week 4.

       

      Tutorials

      In this week's tutorials, we will solve the tutorial questions on the topic of inverse kinematics.

      • Instructions: Please try to solve the tutorial questions on the final few pages of the lecture notes (Task 5.11). Then, please refer to the written answer in Task 5.12, and/or the recorded videos in Task 5.13 to 5.18.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 4.

       

      Workshop

      In this week's workshop hours, you will have time to complete the forward kinematics tasks or the offline programming assignment.

      • Instructions: You will complete the offline programming assignment (5.19) during the workshop. If you wish to work on the group assignment instead, you would need to see a technical staff member to sign out and collect your kit from MPEB 6.02. They will inform you of when to return the kit.
      • Date, time and venue: 
        • Groups 1-10: Monday of Week 5 (11am-1pm), Roberts Building Room 7.04.
        • Groups 11-21: Wednesday of Week 5 (9am-11am), Roberts Building Room 7.04.

       

      Expected learning outcomes

      At the end of this session, participants should:

      • Understand the concept of workspace, existence and multiplicities of solutions.
      • Understand how to calculate the joint space parameters given desired position and orientation of the end-effector or last frame of the robot.

       

       

      Suggested Schedule

      Please complete Tasks 5.1 to 5.10 below, and attempt to solve the tutorial questions (Tasks 5.11 to 5.18) before the workshop  (Tasks 5.19).

    Week 7: Jacobians (LEC & TUT); Inverse Kinematics (WS)

    Overview

    In this week's lecture and tutorial, you will learn how to calculate the velocities of a robot manipulator, as well as the motor torques required for a robot to maintain in equilibrium in view of external forces. You will learn that both the velocities and static forces can be calculated using a matrix called the Jacobians. Then, in the workshop sessions, you will solve the inverse kinematics problem for your robot.

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.


    • Lecture

      In this week's lecture, you will learn about a so-called "Jacobian" matrix, which is used to relate joint velocities and Cartesian velocities, as well as joint torques and Cartesian force in static condition. You will first learn some notations of velocities, followed by a velocity propagation algorithm. Then, another method of direct differentiation will also be explained. There will also be discussion about robot singularities which can be explained using the Jacobian matrix.

      • Instructions: Please watch the video recordings of the lectures, and read the PDF version of the lecture notes. These are labeled as Tasks 7.1 to 7.12 in the links below.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 6.

      Tutorial

      In this week's tutorial, we will solve the questions on Jacobians. 

      • Instructions: Please try to solve the tutorial questions on the final few pages of the lecture notes (Task 7.13). Then, please refer to the written answer in Task 7.14, and/or the recorded videos in Task 7.15 to 7.17.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 6.


      Workshop

      In this week's workshop, you will derive the inverse kinematics of your robot.

      • Instructions: You will go through tasks 7.18 together during the workshop. 
      • Date, time and venue: Monday of Week 7 (11am-1pm) AND Wednesday of Week 7 (9am-11am), MPEB 6th Floor Lab.


      Expected learning outcomes

      At the end of this session, participants should:

      • Understand the relationship between joint velocities and Cartesian velocities, and relationship between joint torque and Cartesian force in static condition.
      • Understand how to calculate the Jacobian matrix using the velocity propagation method, and the direct differentiation method.


      Suggested Schedule

      Please complete Tasks 7.1 to 7.12 below, and attempt to solve the tutorial questions (Tasks 7.13 to 7.17) before the workshop  (Tasks 7.18).

    Week 8: Trajectory Planning (LEC & WS)

    Overview

    In this week's lecture, you will learn how to design the trajectory of a robot, including cubic polynomial, quintic polynomial, and linear functions with parabolic blends. Then in the workshop, you will write your codes to generate the trajectory for your robot to follow.

     

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.


    • Lecture

      In this week's lecture, you will learn about trajectory planning. Specifically, you will learn what trajectory means, and how to generate smooth trajectory profiles including cubic polynomial, quintic polynomial, and linear functions with parabolic blends. 

      • Instructions: Please watch the video recordings of the lectures, and read the PDF version of the lecture notes. These are labeled as Tasks 8.1 to 8.8 in the links below. 
      • Date of video release: Friday of Week 7.

      Workshop

      In this week's workshop, you will continue coding your robot. In particular, you will add in codes to generate smooth trajectory profile for the robot to follow. 

      • Instructions: You will go through tasks 8.9 together during the workshop. 
      • Date, time and venue: Monday of Week 8 (11am-1pm) AND Wednesday of Week 8 (9am-11am), MPEB 6th Floor Lab.

      Expected learning outcomes

      At the end of this session, participants should:

      • Understand the meaning of trajectory, and the difference between joint space scheme and Cartesian space scheme.
      • Understand how to generate smooth trajectory profiles, including cubic polynomial, quintic polynomial, and linear functions with parabolic blends.


      Suggested Schedule

      Please complete Tasks 8.1 to 8.8 below, before the live workshop session (Task 8.9).

    Week 9: Manipulator Dynamics (LEC & TUT); Trajectory Planning (WS)

    Overview

    In this week's lecture and tutorial, you will learn how to derive the dynamics model of a robotic manipulator, using the iterative Newton-Euler formula. You will also learn how to calculate the inertia tensor of a robot, and how to simulate the dynamic behavior of a robot in Matlab. Then, in the workshop sessions, you will continue to solve the trajectory planning problem, and prepare for pick-and-place demo.

     

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.


    • Lecture

      In this week's lecture, you will learn how to derive the dynamic model of a robotic manipulator using the iterative Newton-Euler formula. There will also be discussion on how to include friction force in the model, and how to calculate the model in Cartesian space. Next, you will learn how to calculate the inertia tensor of objects, followed by how to write Matlab code to simulate the dynamic behavior of a robot.

      • Instructions: Please watch the video recordings of the lectures, and read the PDF version of the lecture notes. These are labeled as Tasks 9.1 to 9.15 in the links below.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 8.

      Tutorial

      In this week's tutorial, we will solve the questions on Dynamics. 

      • Instructions: Please try to solve the tutorial questions on the final few pages of the lecture notes (Task 9.16). Then, please refer to the written answer in Task 9.17, and/or the recorded videos in Task9.18 and 9.19.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 8.


      Workshop

      In this week's workshop, you will continue with the trajectory planning problem, and prepare to demonstrate their robots for accomplishing a pick-and-place task.

      • Instructions: You will go through task 9.20 together during the workshop.
      • Date, time and venue: Monday of Week 9 (11am-1pm) AND Wednesday of Week 9 (9am-11am), MPEB 6th Floor Lab.

      Expected learning outcomes

      At the end of this session, participants should:

      • Understand how to derive the dynamic model of a robot, in both joint space and in Cartesian space, and with the inclusion of friction force.
      • Understand how to calculate the inertia tensor of objects.
      • Understand how to write a Matlab code to simulate the dynamic behavior of a robot.


      Suggested Schedule

      Please complete Tasks 9.1 to 9.15 below, and attempt to solve the tutorial questions (Tasks 9.16 to 9.19) before the live session  (Task 9.20).

    Week 10: Manipulator Control (LEC & TUT); Robot Demo (WS)

    Overview

    In this week's lecture and tutorial, you will learn how to design linear and nonlinear controller to control the manipulator. You will then demonstrate your robots for accomplishing a pick-and-place task.

    • Materials and activities

      Required material and activities are numbered to indicate the order in which you should ideally progress through them. A recommended (but approximate) amount of time to spend on each is also highlighted.


    • Lecture

      In this week's lecture, you will learn about control of manipulator. Firstly, we will discuss about control for a second order linear system, followed by control for a single joint. Then, we will discuss about control for a complete manipulator.

      • Instructions: Please watch the video recordings of the lectures, and read the PDF version of the lecture notes. These are labeled as Tasks 10.1 to 10.11 in the links below.
      • Date of video release: Latest by Friday of Week 9.
